key_insight: PEA spacers improve crystal morphology and suppress lattice defects, slowing ambient light- and heat-induced degradation relative to BA spacers in two-dimensional lead iodide perovskites.
engineering_relevance: Spacer selection is a stability design lever for perovskite devices, but should be combined with surface passivation and encapsulation while balancing device performance.
method: Compare BA₂PbI₄ and PEA₂PbI₄ perovskite nanoflakes.
Assess light and thermal stability under ambient conditions.
Probe degradation using confocal micro-Raman and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy.
evidence_signal: Freshly exfoliated samples showed comparable room-temperature luminescence, but PEA-based crystals degraded more slowly despite sharing organic-component loss and decomposition into PbI₂ and metallic Pb.
watch_item: The abstract reports material-level stability improvements, not quantified solar-cell efficiency or operational lifetime gains.
paper_title: Impact of organic spacer cations on the light and thermal stability of two-dimensional lead halide perovskites
